references.text: The first description of the manna that fell along with the dew. Manna was found in the morning when the dew had evaporated, establishing the same pattern described in Numbers 11:9.
God promises to let bread rain down from heaven for the people, fulfilling what is described in Numbers 11:9 about the manna falling on the camp.
A description of the appearance and taste of the manna, providing further context to the heavenly bread that fell as mentioned in Numbers 11:9.
The psalm poetically describes how God opened the doors of heaven and let manna rain down like grain from heaven, the bread of angels, paralleling Numbers 11:9.
Moses reminds the people how God humbled them and fed them with manna, bread that neither they nor their fathers had known. This refers back to the miracle of the manna.
Nehemiah recalls that God gave them bread from heaven when they were hungry, referring to the manna miracle described in Numbers.
Jesus refers to the manna that the fathers ate in the wilderness and explains that it was the Father who gave them the true bread from heaven, a direct link to the Old Testament text about manna.
Jesus contrasts the manna that the fathers ate in the wilderness with himself as the living bread from heaven, pointing to the miracle of the manna.
Paul mentions that all the Israelites ate the same spiritual food, referring to the manna in the wilderness.
The promise of hidden manna to the one who overcomes, alluding to the manna miracle and its spiritual significance.
